issues.description: SealSaloon constructor signature is inconsistent between the problem statement and the code artifacts. The problem statement (UML and textual description) requires a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name (problem_statement.md: line 29 and line 71). However, the solution implementation defines a no-argument constructor public SealSaloon() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java: line 8) and the template/example usage in Main instantiates SealSaloon with no arguments (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java: line 11). This mismatch will confuse students about whether they must implement a constructor that takes a name and whether a name field/getter is required; it may also cause tests or grading checks that expect SealSaloon(String) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Preferred fix: implement the constructor SealSaloon(String name) in the SealSaloon class, add a private final String name field and a public getter for it, and update example usages in Main to call new SealSaloon("SomeName"). Alternatively, if the intended design is a no-argument constructor, update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to require a no-arg constructor. The preferred option is to update the code to match the current specification (add the String-parameter constructor and name field/getter).
